problem: health run records coverage whenever its data was applied; health baseline update (and its module/file refusal) still uses measuredSources(latest.sources), which omits coverage applied while disabled. Also raised by review-regression (R5-B01), review-logic (F-001) and review-testing-practices (R5-T01).
impact: A re-baseline drops coverage while its penalty stays in the scores; the next run folds it out again, and a real 30-point eslint regression reads reg 5 / WARN instead of reg 30 / FAIL.
suggested_fix: One scored-sources rule, persisted in the report and read by both writers and the refusal.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every reader and writer of the recorded source set (writeBaseline, foldNewSources, recordBaselineSources, loadBaselineSources, measuredSources callers) via keryx ctx rg over src/health.

verification.evidence: probe-coverage-rebaseline retargeted, `disabled`: after updateBaseline sources drop coverage; unchanged run2 reg -25 improved, baseline 75 -> 50; run4 with 3 eslint errors warn health 45 reg 5. Control `import`: sources keep coverage, run2 reg 0, run4 fail reg 30.

problem: No test folds coverage as the new source; dropping newCoveragePenalty from the effect leaves the suite green.
impact: A coverage report appearing on a baselined project could fold nothing, and its penalty would later read as a regression of unchanged code.
suggested_fix: Integration test: baseline without coverage, report appears, first and second runs regression 0.
evidence: Mutant E06 green (188 pass). Verifier: confirmed.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every coverage test read: none starts with a baseline and then adds a report.

verification.evidence: scopes.ts effect with newRisk only: bun test --timeout 30000 src/health 188 pass, 0 fail. Restored.

problem: Coverage is recorded when its source is `available` even if no data was applied (e.g. coverage-final.json only).
impact: A later coverage-summary.json fails unchanged code with regression 15.
suggested_fix: Decide coverage membership by applied data alone.

problem: A coverage report the baseline measured can disappear; the lost penalty reads as an improvement and hides drift of the same size. Pre-existing, applies to any vanished source.
impact: Drift up to the coverage penalty hidden while the report is absent.
suggested_fix: Keep the penalty on the comparison side, or WARN when a baseline-measured source produced no data. Deferral acceptable if tracked.

problem: The line turning the refusal into the process exit status is untested.
impact: Deleting it makes a refusal exit 0 with CI green.
Per-file coverage could shape scores while unrecorded.
suggested_fix: Test a summary with per-file entries and no total.

problem: The damaged-JSON branch of the single baseline parser is untested.
impact: A change to throw would crash every health run on a truncated scores.json.

problem: Internal fold accounting on the persisted ScopeMetrics; relative to the baseline at run time. Also: the per-LOC formula is duplicated from healthScore (R5-A03).
impact: Report contract grew an undocumented, stale-able field; two copies of the scoring formula.
suggested_fix: Side channel from computeMetrics; export normalizedPenalty from scoring.ts.

problem: A `file:` baseline entry with no findings in the fold run is not folded even if a new coverage source penalises it.
impact: File-scope trend/regression only, once per file.
suggested_fix: Accept and document, or fold every baseline file key.
